tumor buds: Small clusters of tumor cells at the invasive front, detached from the main tumor mass.
simple gland: A round or tubular epithelial structure with a central lumen, lined by a single layer of cells.
primary mucinous adenocarcinoma: Abundant extracellular mucin pools containing floating tumor cells with signet-ring morphology.
primary lung cancers: A malignant tumor nodule with glandular or squamous differentiation invading lung parenchyma.
cd4 cells: Small lymphocytes with round dark nuclei and scant cytoplasm, indistinguishable from other T-cells on H&E.

concept: remodeled airway with no alveoli present and collagen/fibrosis around them
encoded_text: remodeled airway with no alveoli present and collagen/fibrosis around them: A distorted bronchiole surrounded by dense eosinophilic collagenous stroma, lacking adjacent alveolar spaces.

concept: obstructive pneumonia or atelectasis leading to lung collapse
encoded_text: obstructive pneumonia or atelectasis leading to lung collapse: Alveolar spaces collapsed with crowded septa, foamy macrophages, and mucus plugs.
bronchial region: A large airway with cartilage plates, respiratory epithelium, and smooth muscle bundles.
bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue: Submucosal aggregate of lymphocytes, often with a germinal center, adjacent to a bronchus.
mucoid degeneration: Amorphous basophilic mucinous material replacing stroma, with stellate fibroblasts.
basal lamina collagen: Thin eosinophilic band beneath epithelial cells, often thickened in fibrosis.
tumor-associated macrophages: Large cells with abundant foamy or granular cytoplasm amidst tumor cells.
small adenocarcinoma areas: Tiny glands or clusters of malignant cells with atypical nuclei infiltrating lung parenchyma.
morphologic findings: The overall appearance of cells and tissue structures under the microscope.
intramucosal: Crowded atypical epithelial cells confined within the mucosa, above the basement membrane.

concept: spindle-shaped cells with atypical nuclei and vesicular growth pattern
encoded_text: spindle-shaped cells with atypical nuclei and vesicular growth pattern: Elongated cells with pleomorphic nuclei and bubbly cytoplasmic vacuoles, often in sarcomatoid tumors.
air sac: Thin-walled alveolar spaces lined by flat pneumocytes, filled with air or fluid.
darkly stained circular nucleus: Small round hyperchromatic nucleus, often of a lymphocyte or small cell carcinoma cell.
myxoid transformation: Abundant pale basophilic myxoid matrix with sparse spindle or stellate cells.
